images.alt: A tall painted wooden shield from North Queensland, photographed against a plain background in a museum
images.caption: A North Queensland shield in the Ethnological Museum, Berlin, collected in 1913: the big painted plank cut from a buttress flange, of the kind Roth described at the Tully and the Bloomfield.
images.credit: Photograph: FA2010, Wikimedia Commons; object in the Ethnological Museum, Berlin (Edlinger collection, 1913)

images.alt: A painted wooden rainforest shield with a central boss, from north-eastern Queensland, in a museum photograph
images.caption: Shield, mid to late 19th century, north-eastern Queensland, wood and paint, 77.5 by 36.2 cm; the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (1979.206.1802). The central boss and the painted design are the rainforest pattern.
images.credit: Photograph: the Metropolitan Museum of Art, via Wikimedia Commons
images.location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
